page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E4.Flex.2-32 is a flexible virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7J13 processor built on the x86_64 architecture. The configuration supplies 4 dedicated virtual CPUs running at a base clock speed of 2.55 GHz, derived from 2 physical cores operating at 2 threads per core. System memory is provisioned at 32.0 GB, establishing an allocation of 8.0 GB of memory per core and an overall 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio.

The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, requiring external block storage for operating system installations and persistent data storage. No discrete graphics hardware or accelerator units are bundled with this instance type. Network provisioning includes one complimentary public IPv4 address for external connectivity.

With a high memory-to-compute ratio, the instance provides qualitative cost efficiency for systems constrained primarily by memory capacity rather than parallel computing throughput. It delivers predictable compute performance through dedicated CPU thread pinning while avoiding overhead associated with unneeded execution cores. Primary workload fits include in-memory key-value stores, relational databases, data transformation jobs, and backend services with high resident memory footprints.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E4.Flex.2-32 is a memory-oriented virtual machine configuration within the Standard family. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7J13 processor running at 2.55 GHz, it supplies 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. It features 32.0 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage or GPU accelerators, relying on external network-attached volumes for persistent data. One complimentary public IPv4 address is provided. By packaging a relatively large memory pool with a moderate core count, VM.Standard.E4.Flex.2-32 optimizes resource efficiency for operations where working memory capacity dictates sizing rather than parallel compute power. This hardware configuration is suited for in-memory caches, relational database instances, memory-heavy microservices, and lightweight data transformation pipelines.
